function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

The user wants two searches:

1. In New York (NY) find Italian restaurants with vegetarian options.

2. In Los Angeles (LA) find Japanese sushi restaurants with delivery service.

We need to call the function twice. The function signature expects location string, cuisine string, preferences optional array of strings. For first: location "New York, NY", cuisine "Italian", preferences ["Vegetarian"]. For second: location "Los Angeles, CA" or "Los Angeles, CA"? The user said Los Angeles; we can use "Los Angeles, CA". Cuisine "Japanese" or "Sushi"? The function expects cuisine type like "Japanese". Preferences ["Delivery"].

We should call the function twice. But the tool only allows one function call per response? Actually we can call multiple times but each call returns a result. We might need to do separate calls. According to guidelines, we can call the function once per response. But we can combine into one? The function signature only accepts one set of arguments. So we need to make two separate calls. We can either chain them sequentially: first call, then second call. But the guidelines say we can only call one function at a time. However we can produce multiple calls in sequence if needed. But we need to respond with the function call JSON. We cannot output text before calling the function. So we need to decide which search to do first. Maybe we can do the first search: location "New York, NY", cuisine "Italian", preferences ["Vegetarian"]. Then after receiving results, we can call again for LA. But the user asked for both. We could ask clarifying question: "Which city would you like me to search first?" But we can also just do the first search. But the user specifically wants both. We can do the first search now, then after returning results, we can do the second. That means we will have two responses: first function call, then second function call. That's acceptable.

Thus we will first call the function for New York.
